overall: Los Angeles is experiencing a classic June marine layer pattern with patchy fog clearing by mid-morning and mostly cloudy skies limiting solar heating. As of ~10:20 ET, the running max sits at 64.4°F with a modest warming velocity of +1.8°F/hr, though acceleration has turned negative (-0.9°F/hr²) suggesting the warming rate is already decelerating. The extreme heat alerts in the region are confined to inland deserts (San Diego County Deserts, Phoenix area) and do not directly influence the coastal LA TMAX station, which is under a cool southwest marine flow.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show moderate agreement with a range of 67.0–70.2°F (NBM=67.0, ECMWF=68.4, HRRR=70.2), clustering near the NWS official forecast of 69°F. Observed temperatures are running slightly below the D1_PRIOR model expectations for this time of day, consistent with the cloud cover and marine influence keeping the early morning cooler than a typical sunny June pattern.
max_temp_prediction: With ~4–6 hours of warming remaining before the expected peak (models target 14.7–16.7h ET), the temperature needs roughly 4–5°F more to reach the NWS-forecast 69°F target — achievable at the current rate despite decelerating momentum. The META model assigns the highest single-bucket probability to 70–71°F (21.6%), broadly consistent with the NWP model mean of ~68.5°F and the NWS call of 69°F; moderate cloud cover is the primary factor capping the upside. Best estimate is approximately 69.5°F, with meaningful uncertainty spanning roughly 67–72°F given the cloudy marine layer and slowing warming trend.
